item.title: Aaron Rodgers, Steelers totally tank in primetime as Cincinnati Bengals roll to 38-18 Scorigami win
item.description: Joe Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns while Ja'Marr Chase hauled in 231 yards as the Bengals demolished the Steelers 38-18.
item.content:encoded:
Primetime turned into Scorigami time.

The Bengals beat the brakes off Pittsburgh 38-18 on Sunday night to grab first place in the AFC North.

And in over 100 years of NFL history, no game had ever ended with that exact score (i.e., Scorigami!). That gave the NFL two Scorigamis on the same day after San Francisco's 46-40 win over the Cowboys earlier in the afternoon.

Heading into Sunday night, the Bengals and Steelers both sat at 6-2 on four-game winning streaks, with Pittsburgh holding the division tiebreaker from Week 3.

But it was over by halftime.

STEELERS AND BENGALS MEET IN AFC NORTH SHOWDOWN ON SUNDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL WITH BOTH TEAMS AT 6-2

Even with an entire bye week to prepare against a Bengals team flying back from Madrid, Pittsburgh had zero answers in stopping Joe Burrow and the Cincy offense.

Cincinnati built a 24-3 halftime lead, pushed it to 31-3, and didn't punt until the final minute of the third quarter.

BEST SPORTSBOOK PROMOS FOR SUNDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL: BENGALS VS STEELERS OFFERS

Things got so lopsided that Cincinnati pulled Joe Burrow with seven minutes left in the fourth for 41-year-old backup Joe Flacco, while Pittsburgh needed two garbage-time touchdowns from DK Metcalf and Pat Freiermuth just to dress up the scoreboard and produce the first 38-18 final score in NFL history.

Sunday also proved how hollow Pittsburgh's 6-2 start really was. Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh offense couldn't even move the chains until the second quarter. Rodgers didn't survive until the final whistle as Mason Rudolph stepped in to relieve the 42-year-old future Hall of Famer.

'WHAT THE F--K, CALL IT!': AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY CURSE AT EACH OTHER DURING HOT MIC MOMENT

Cincinnati showed what a 6-2 contender with legit Super Bowl upside plays like.

Burrow carved up Pittsburgh's defense for 409 yards and four touchdowns, while Ja'Marr Chase hauled in 11 passes for 231 yards, outgaining Pittsburgh's entire offense all by himself.

JD VANCE SEES BENGALS MAKING 'A RUN' BUT THAT'S UNDERSTANDABLE BECAUSE HE'S A FAN, ESPECIALLY OF JA'MARR CHASE

On the other side of the ball, Dexter Lawrence kept building his Defensive Player of the Year case, anchoring a front that flat-out suffocated Pittsburgh's run game.

Three weeks ago, Cincinnati went into Baltimore and embarrassed the Ravens.

Sunday night, the Bengals did the exact same thing to Pittsburgh, proving the AFC North runs through Cincinnati.

Even Sopranos star Steven Van Zandt, famous for playing consigliere Silvio Dante, had seen enough of Mike McCarthy's squad, firing off a reaction:

"The Steelers are embarrassing themselves. I never liked this coach. I thought he was terrible in Dallas. I couldn't believe they hired him in Pittsburgh. There's two ways to prove you're a good team. Come out with a good scheme. Or adjust it when necessary. Let's see if they adjust it for the second half. If they don't, some mamajama needs to be fired."

Capisce!

item.title: 49ers fans involved in second consecutive week of fighting after Cowboys game at AT&T Stadium
item.description: Video captures a massive brawl between San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys fans at Texas Live, where police scrambled to break up the chaos.
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco 49ers fans were very present at AT&T Stadium on Sunday as they faced the Dallas Cowboys– two heated rivals in the NFL.

That rivalry spilled over in a very bad way with a massive brawl taking place at Texas Live, a large entertainment complex just outside the stadium between supporters of both fan bases after the 49ers’ 46-40 win in Week 10.

Police had to get involved to break things up, and likely book some people into the local jail as video from Dallas Texas TV social media accounts showcased the brutal altercation.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The video began with two police officers subduing one fan on the ground, though a fight continued to occur next to them.

A 49ers fan was seen tossing punches at a Cowboys fan, who was clearly fighting back. Some others around the incident were trying to break it up, but a quick camera pan showed another fight seemingly being de-escalated by a Cowboys fan restraining a 49ers fan who had been fighting.

Then, as police were escorting a fan away from the tense scene, another skirmish broke out. There were two women, one wearing a 49ers jacket and the other in Cowboys gear, were in each other’s faces as shoving seemed to be going on.

While it’s unclear what exactly caused the brawls to take place, 49ers fans have not been helping their reputation after what happened last week as they played another rival, the Las Vegas Raiders, at home in Santa Clara.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

A massive parking lot brawl broke out last weekend between 49ers and Raiders fans, with one video going viral after fans were knocked out while throwing punches.

Nearly a dozen people were arrested and 45 were ejected from Levi’s Stadium for fighting, Santa Clara police told SF Gate.

"Incidents of violence at large-scale events in Santa Clara will not be tolerated," Santa Clara Police Department spokesperson Lt. Eric Lagergren told the outlet. "The Department strictly enforces the law and holds individuals accountable for criminal conduct. We will seek to arrest the individuals responsible for the fan-on-fan violence at the event."

Seven of the 11 people who were arrested were cited for disorderly conduct. Four were arrested for allegedly fighting in a public place and at least one received a drug possession charge.

It’s unknown how many arrests and ejections there may have been at AT&T Stadium, but these teams and fan bases certainly do not like each other and that is very apparent each time they match up during an NFL season.

Fox News’ Ryan Gaydos contributed to this report.

item.title: 49ers offense puts up over 580 yards against a bad Cowboys defense behind a Christian McCaffrey masterclass
item.description: Kaelon Black's bulldozing TD and Deebo Samuel's 70-yard reverse blew open a tight game as the San Francisco 49ers torched Dallas for 584 yards.
item.content:encoded:
If there's a sole team above the rest in the NFL, it's the San Francisco 49ers.

San Francisco improved to 8-1 on Sunday with a 46-40 win at AT&T Stadium, piling up 584 total yards as red jerseys outnumbered and out-yelled home fans.

It was a close battle until the third quarter when a pair of electric Niners rushing touchdowns stuffed the Cowboys in a deep hole.

CHRISTIAN MCCAFFREY GIVES ONE 49ERS QUALITY THAT SEPARATES TEAM FROM PACK AMID SUPER BOWL HOPES

Rookie Kaelon Black sparked the surge on the opening drive of the second half, lowering his shoulder to bulldoze two Cowboys defenders, including first-round pick Caleb Downs and cornerback Cobie Durant, on his way to a 25-yard scamper.

Moments later, the seasoned second-term Niners star, Deebo Samuel Sr., stuck the dagger in Dallas on a 70-yard reverse, taking a pitch from Black.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

On Sunday, San Francisco piled on 214 rushing yards: Black finished with 53 yards on 11 carries, while Samuel totaled 78 rushing yards on three carries in his first game back since Oct. 11, alongside an 11-yard touchdown catch.

Christian McCaffrey added three touchdowns of his own, including 74- and 66-yard catch-and-runs, as the 49ers averaged more than 9 yards a play.

"Totally unacceptable defense," Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said after the loss.

San Francisco's offensive clinic ruined a gutsy outing from Dak Prescott, who did everything possible to keep Dallas alive. Prescott threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns, hitting George Pickens three times in the end zone.

COWBOYS HIRE LONGTIME NFL COACH OUT OF RETIREMENT TO ADDRESS TEAM'S BRUTAL DEFENSIVE START

But Prescott's best efforts couldn't survive the defensive disaster led by first-year coordinator Christian Parker, who looked completely out of his depth as Kyle Shanahan picked Dallas apart for the most home yards allowed in franchise history.

item.title: Mike Vrabel doesn't want Patriots to 'b---h and complain' but he b----es and complains about his players a lot
item.description: Mike Vrabel says winners don't complain, but his post-loss press conference in Munich told a very different story after the Patriots' 35-10 defeat.
item.content:encoded:
After his New England Patriots were demolished by the Detroit Lions in Munich on Sunday, coach Mike Vrabel told reporters he doesn't want to hear anyone "b---h and complain" because that's what "losers" do.

Except that if you listen to Vrabel, especially after that 35-10 loss, he did a lot of what he doesn't want to hear others do — b---h and complain.

DRAKE MAYE TELLS REPORTERS THEY DON'T KNOW 'WHAT THEY'RE TALKING ABOUT' DURING GERMANY PRESS CONFERENCE

In one news conference, Vrabel suggested losing quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury probably had no effect on the outcome of the game.

In other words, having his starting quarterback wouldn't have helped the Patriots much.

"I don't think Drake's being in there or not would have really helped," Vrabel said. "I mean, it may have. I would highly doubt it, until we start doing the little things better in all three phases, the fundamentals, being able to run the football, being able to get open and catch and protect our quarterback, tackle, get off the field on third down, create turnovers."

Vrabel complained the New England defense provides only "glimpses" of what it's supposed to deliver, particularly the last two weeks when it has given up 80 combined points to the Lions and Green Bay Packers.

"Give up too many plays, too many missed tackles, too many clean pockets for the quarterback, and don't affect them," Vrabel said.

Look, the Patriots got out-classed the last two weeks. So it is understandable Vrabel doesn't love the way his players are performing lately.

His frustration makes perfect sense.

But it seems Vrabel never complains about his coaching staff. He never laments bad play-calls or preparation. It's always on the players.

And it happens a lot.

DRAKE MAYE VOICES SUPPORT FOR PATRIOTS COACH MIKE VRABEL AS OFF-FIELD CONTROVERSY CONTINUES TO SWIRL

A couple of weeks ago, Vrabel complained about the play of cornerback Christian Gonzalez. It seemed fair because Gonzalez didn't perform, but did anyone hear any attention placed on the secondary coach? Or the defensive coordinator?

After the Super Bowl last season, a game in which the Patriots yielded six sacks, Vrabel never suggested his offensive coaches got out-coached. Never said rookie left tackle Will Campbell might have benefited from some help.

He instead talked about how the sacks were "on the quarterback" or "somebody got beat."

Oh, and by the way, last spring when running back TreVeyon Henderson publicly defended Bulls player Jaden Ivey over his opinions about LGBTQ issues, Vrabel's default position was not to defend Henderson.

Vrabel instead pushed back on Henderson's judgment by stressing the player needed to consider how he represents the team and whether he's fully educated on topics he comments about.

The irony, of course, is that days later, Vrabel's representation of the team would be very much in question when his relationship with Dianna Russini became public.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

To be fair, Vrabel, on Sunday, did shoulder some responsibility for how his team is playing. But he soon added others to the group.

"I'm not going to, again, we've gotten beat two weeks in a row," he said. "That starts with me, and again, we're professionals. We're grown men. We all have to recognize what it is, we need to do better and improve. That's what winners do.

"Winners figure out ways to help the team win. They don't b---h and complain. They try to find ways to help the team."

item.title: Young paraglider dies after reported emergency sends him crashing into field during Illinois flight
item.description: Officials are investigating a fatal paragliding incident involving a 21-year-old man from a Chicago suburb who shared his aerial adventures and daring stunts online.
item.content:encoded:
An Illinois paraglider died in a weekend crash after reportedly experiencing an emergency mid-flight.

Officials on Saturday identified the victim as Giovanni Lopez, 21, of Woodridge, a southwest suburb of Chicago.

Lopez frequently documented his paragliding adventures and daring aerial maneuvers on social media.

The Kendall County Coroner’s Office said it was notified around 3:40 p.m. Saturday of a possible fatality in Plainfield, an area dotted with farm fields southwest of Chicago.

CLIMBER STRANDED ON 6-INCH LEDGE AT 11,000 FEET AS 46 MPH WINDS GROUND RESCUE HELICOPTER

"The Kendall County Coroner’s Office was notified of a possible fatality related to a paragliding incident in the area of Ridge Road and 127th Street in Plainfield, Illinois," the office said.

Officials did not disclose the exact circumstances that led to Lopez’s death.

NBC Chicago reported that Lopez encountered an emergency while paragliding.

HIKER IDENTIFIED, POPULAR TRAIL CLOSED AFTER DEADLY FALL AT UTAH'S ZION NATIONAL PARK

Witnesses reportedly rushed to Lopez's aid and attempted to help him until paramedics arrived and continued lifesaving efforts, the outlet said.

Upon arrival, coroner’s deputies pronounced Lopez dead at the scene.

Officials said the cause and manner of death will be determined following a forensic autopsy.

The incident remains under investigation by the Plainfield Police Department and the Kendall County Coroner's Office.

Additional agencies assisted in the investigation, including the Oswego Fire Protection District and the Kendall County Sheriff's Office.

item.title: Pete Buttigieg breaks with Democrats on student loan handouts, admits party ‘overtorqued’ on issue
item.description: Pete Buttigieg said the Democratic Party "overtorqued" on student loans, admitting that he struggles to justify loan forgiveness to non-college relatives.
item.content:encoded:
Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg admitted Sunday that he broke ranks with the Democratic Party on student loans, saying the party "overtorqued" the issue and may have dissuaded voters.

During a "Pod Save America" interview, host Dan Pfeiffer remarked that many of the Democratic candidates who won in the midterm elections disagreed with the party on at least one issue, whether it be gun control or the role of oil and gas in energy.

He asked Buttigieg whether he held any beliefs that ran counter to the mainstream Democratic Party.

BERNIE SANDERS ADMITS DEMOCRATS FAILED WORKING-CLASS VOTERS ON ECONOMICS, DRIVING THEM TO DONALD TRUMP

"In the 2020 campaign, I definitely staked out some positions that I still believe in that weren't always kind of popular in the party," Buttigieg said. "One thing is, I think...we really overtorqued on the student loan thing. As a party, I have a very hard time explaining to my relatives in Michigan who did not go to college why they should be paying for people who do."

He added, "I believe there are ways to make sure that you come out of college debt-free. I believe college should be more affordable. I don't believe in like a magic wand to fix that for everybody who borrowed money."

PETE BUTTIGIEG DISTANCES HIMSELF FROM BIDEN AMID 2028 TALK, SUGGESTS 'BUILD BACK BETTER' DOESN'T WORK

Though Buttigieg told Pfeiffer that he doesn't believe in a "magic" fix for student loans, he previously served under President Joe Biden, who repeatedly attempted to cancel student loan debt, even after the Supreme Court ruled against his administration in 2023.

His husband, Chasten Buttigieg, was also among those frustrated at the prospect of paying student loans after COVID-19-era loan relief was set to expire in 2022.

Fox News Digital reached out to Buttigieg's organization, Win the Era, for comment.

Veteran Democratic strategist Julian Epstein called the student loan forgiveness a scam and congratulated Buttigieg for having enough self-awareness to acknowledge it.

JOE MANCHIN WARNS DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ARE GAINING GROUND AS DEMOCRATS REMAIN SILENT

"Buttigieg shows an all-too-rare self-awareness for a Democrat elite on this issue. The student loan giveaway, also known as loan forgiveness, is a scam," Epstein told Fox News Digital. "It's welfare for the most privileged and elite amongst us that the working class has to help fund. It's Robin Hood in reverse, and it stands against everything the Democratic Party should be standing for."

Another issue Buttigieg disagreed with the Democratic Party on was the two-party system itself.

"That makes some Democratic organizations nervous when you talk that way, but I think that a lot of the problems we've had around polarization, gerrymandering, even some of what goes on with money would be better if we were actually a healthy multi-party democracy," Buttigieg said.

item.title: Raiders fans stayed seated when Fernando Mendoza scored so his wheelchair bound mom could see him celebrate
item.description: Las Vegas Raiders fans stayed seated after Fernando Mendoza's first NFL touchdown so his mother, who battles multiple sclerosis, could watch.
item.content:encoded:
Las Vegas Raiders fans have a certain reputation after being featured in parking lot brawls with other fans and showing themselves as often unforgiving with ownership, coaching and their own players. But Fernando Mendoza is in his honeymoon period.

So he not only gets special treatment, but graceful treatment that extends to his family.

The rookie first-round pick got his first NFL start on Sunday and Raiders fans came out to Allegiant Stadium prepared to support not only their new quarterback but to also sow amazing grace to his family.

VIKINGS ACQUIRE KIRK COUSINS FROM RAIDERS WHO TURN TO FERNANDO MENDOZA AS THEIR STARTING QB

How?

Before the game, there were fans carrying signs around the stadium reminding others not to stand if Mendoza scored or otherwise made a big play.

And the reason is they wanted to make sure Mendoza's mom, Elsa Mendoza would be able to see the play and the reaction.

Elsa Mendoza, you should know, has been battling multiple sclerosis (MS) , a chronic degenerative disease that affects the central nervous system, for nearly two decades.

FERNANDO MENDOZA, THE NO 1 PICK OF NFL DRAFT TO THE RAIDERS, TASKED WITH RETURNING A LEGACY FRANCHISE TO GLORY

Her condition – along with complications following a severe bout with COVID-19 years ago – has progressively affected her physical mobility, requiring her to use a wheelchair and limiting her ability to freely walk, travel, and navigate stairs independently without assistance.

Also, in short, she struggles to get to her feet.

So when Mendoza scored his first NFL touchdown on a 10 yard run in Sunday's first quarter against the Seahawks, many fans remained in their seats.

And some who rose, quickly sat back down.

All of that so Elsa Mendoza, watching from a suite with the rest of the Mendoza family, could see her son celebrate.

"Super grateful to the Silver and Black for doing that," Mendoza said after the game. "Means a lot to my family and I. And I just can't thank you guys enough.

"On a dark day it brings a smile to my face so I really thank everybody for respecting my family. I appreciate all the support."

item.title: Mexico's cartel 'godfather' convicted in American DEA agent's murder dies at age 80
item.description: The Guadalajara cartel boss convicted in DEA agent Enrique "Kiki" Camarena's murder died at 80, decades after the killing triggered Operation Leyenda.
item.content:encoded:
The Mexican cartel boss who helped build a drug empire supplying the United States and was convicted in the murder of Drug Enforcement Administration agent Enrique "Kiki" Camarena has died at 80.

Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, known as the "boss of bosses," died Sunday in a Guadalajara hospital after suffering multiple organ failure, The Associated Press reported, citing Jalisco’s security ministry. He had been transferred from prison Friday.

Felix Gallardo had been behind bars since 1989, according to The AP.

JOHN KOUFOS: TRUMP’S ‘SHIELD OF THE AMERICAS’ COULD HELP DEFEND US FROM CARTELS

His death comes more than four decades after Camarena’s abduction and torture, a killing that sparked the largest homicide investigation in DEA history, according to the agency.

In 2017, a Mexican federal judge gave Felix Gallardo a 37-year prison term for the murders of Camarena and Mexican pilot Alfredo Zavala, Excélsior reported. The judge also ordered more than 20 million pesos in compensation for the victims’ families, roughly $1.18 million at the time.

Camarena was heading to meet his wife for lunch on Feb. 7, 1985, when five men abducted him as he left the U.S. Consulate in Guadalajara, according to the DEA. One of the attackers identified himself as a Mexican law enforcement official.

DRUG CARTEL KINGPIN AMONG TARGETS IN SWEEPING TRUMP CRACKDOWN ON ALLEGED MEXICAN CORRUPTION NETWORK

The 37-year-old agent was never seen alive again.

The DEA says Camarena was believed to have been tortured for two days before dying from a crushed skull. His body was discovered on March 5, 1985.

His killing triggered Operation Leyenda, which the agency describes as the largest homicide investigation it had ever undertaken. Felix Gallardo was among the major Mexican crime figures arrested in connection with Camarena’s torture and murder, according to the DEA.

ICE RENEWS HUNT FOR EL CHAPO'S LAST TWO FUGITIVE SONS WITH MASSIVE REWARD

The agent, a Marine Corps veteran who joined the DEA in 1974, left behind his wife and three children.

Felix Gallardo’s reach helped reshape organized crime in Mexico. A 2023 report released by Sen. Chuck Grassley’s office described the former police officer as having brought traffickers together into a large organization that became a blueprint for many of Mexico’s major criminal groups.

EXCLUSIVE: INSIDE TRUMP'S CARTEL CRACKDOWN AS WHITE HOUSE OFFICIAL DETAILS PRESIDENT'S PRIVATE BRIEFINGS

The Guadalajara cartel was among the first Mexican trafficking organizations to work with Colombian cocaine suppliers, according to a historical DEA publication. The agency said Felix Gallardo and Rafael Caro Quintero formed the cartel to ship heroin and marijuana into the United States before it prospered from the cocaine trade.

Camarena’s legacy, meanwhile, lives on through the red ribbons worn each October in his memory as part of drug prevention efforts, according to the DEA.

Fox News Digital reached out to Jalisco’s security ministry and the DEA for confirmation and comment.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Lane Kiffin blames LSU's $40+ million roster after loss to Texas: 'we'll have better rosters’
item.description: Lane Kiffin blamed LSU's roster after losing to the Texas Longhorns despite forcing three Arch Manning interceptions and dominating key stats.
item.content:encoded:
When Lane Kiffin made the choice to leave Ole Miss late in the 2025 college football season for the LSU Tigers, one of his primary motivations was to coach in the College Football Playoff. Late in the 2026 college football season, he's about to make it two straight years of not coaching in the College Football Playoff.

LSU took its fourth loss of the season on Saturday night, falling to the Texas Longhorns despite an atrocious performance from quarterback Arch Manning, and an overwhelming statistical advantage. It was the latest in a season full of similar losses, where LSU outplays the opposition and still loses.

ESPN analyst Bill Connelly, creator of the SP+ ranking system, has an "postgame win expectancy" based on elements within a game that are most under team control: success rate, yards per play, explosives, field position, and turnovers. LSU's postgame win expectancy in the loss to Kentucky was 65.5%. Against Texas, it was 66.5%. They lost both.

ARCH MANNING DELIVERS ICE-COLD QUOTE AFTER TEXAS CLOSES DOOR ON LSU'S COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF DREAMS

LSU had 5.5 yards per play offensively, and allowed just 4.1 to Texas. They had four sacks and six tackles for loss, and forced three interceptions from Manning. But a number of mistakes from Sam Leavitt and missed opportunities in the red zone doomed the Tigers.

Most long-time fans of college football are used to such losses, and putting the blame for them on the coaching staff. Losing this many close games is a function of randomness, to be sure, but when the randomness tilts this frequently in one direction, it's worth at least opening up the discussion that the coaches deserve some, if not most, of the blame.

But Kiffin, in his news conference after the loss, took a bit of a different path, choosing instead to blame the players. Kinda.

"We’ll have better rosters, and that’s no poor reflection upon these players," Kiffin said. "We just will. We will have been here. We’ll have built depth. We will. We won’t have senior days with two scholarship players."

No "poor reflection" on the players, he says, but they're bad, and we'll have better ones in the coming seasons. How else is anyone listening supposed to take that? Including the players themselves.

This is, remember, a roster that LSU spent an estimated $40-$50 million on, a level of spending that was a major factor in getting Kiffin to bolt for Baton Rouge. The Tigers and their boosters were willing to commit to resources that Ole Miss either wouldn't or couldn't match. The thinking being that consistent success would come from better players. The same players that he's now throwing under the bus.

To be fair to the 51-year-old coach, he did admit that he should get some blame too.

"I get it," Kiffin said. "Underperformance. It doesn't matter if the games have been close or if they go down to the last six seconds. I was brought here to win, and we need to win more than that."

But then he brought it back to the roster again, saying, "Now also everything isn't built for the first year when you come in somewhere and I would tell you if we were undefeated right now, you know, you build things and they take a little bit of time..."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

It's interesting, because after the Tigers beat up on a hapless Clemson team, Kiffin sarcastically said in the postgame interview just "imagine if we had pro players." So when LSU looked unstoppable in Week 1, he was so confident in his roster that he sarcastically referred to needing "pro players." Now that they're 6-4 and 3-4 in the SEC, he needs time to build the $40-$50 million roster up. Wonder what changed.

He is right, however, to point out that these close games that come down to the final few seconds can hinge on one play or one bounce going a slightly different way.

"Yes, we need to win games," Kiffin said. "But I also don't overreact. If we covered a guy on that last play or if that fumble comes out a second earlier or whatever, we're in here and none of these questions are happening, and you're like, 'What a great job! What an awesome way to finish.'"

Win the Kentucky game and this Texas game, and the Tigers are 8-2 and likely heading for the College Football Playoff. But they didn't win those games. Part of that is on the players, yes, but plenty of it is on the coaches too. Again, LSU is not just spending $40-50 million on the roster, they're also spending $90+ million on Kiffin, a buyout to Brian Kelly, $3 million per season on defensive coordinator Blake Baker, $2.5 million per season on Charlie Weiss Jr., and $800,000 on their strength and conditioning coach. The total salary of the support staff around Kiffin is around $14.6 million.

And for that, in each game where LSU's led and arguably should have won, they didn't.

Entering the fourth quarter, with the Tigers up 21-13, their offensive drives went like this:

That's 15 plays for -1 yard, at home, in the fourth quarter of a season-changing game. When your head coach is supposed to be an offensive mastermind, that's just not good enough.

Kiffin's rosters probably will be better moving forward, and he's right that LSU can feel like they've been unlucky this season to get the results they've had. But it's worth wondering how many years of grace he'll get in Baton Rouge, how much more NIL money will be available until the well dries up. Particularly if the results don't match the salaries.

If it doesn't turn around in 2027, LSU might turn their $200 million debacle into an even bigger one.

item.title: Massive fire erupts outside MetLife Stadium after Bills defeat Jets in Week 10
item.description: Video shows flames and thick black smoke billowing over MetLife Stadium near the adjacent train station after the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets.
item.content:encoded:
A massive fire erupted outside of MetLife Stadium on Sunday night hours after the Buffalo Bills defeated the New York Jets, 31-12, in Week 10.

Flames and thick, black smoke were billowing near the train station adjacent to MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. 

Sergeant First Class Charles Marchan of the New Jersey State Police told OutKick in a statement that troopers responded to a report of smoke around 5:51 p.m. outside the stadium "adjacent to Lot A, next to the AMEX gate in the postgame tent."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"Upon arrival, troopers observed visible flames," Marchan wrote in a statement. "At the time of the fire, the tent was unoccupied. NJSEA, Moonachie and Carlstadt fire personnel arrived on scene and extinguished the fire. 

"No damage was reported to any additional structures, and no injuries were reported on scene. The cause of the fire is currently under investigation. No additional information is available at this time."

It was initially reported as a "structure fire," per ESPN Jets reporter Rich Cimini.

"People told not to go near the east plaza of the stadium (train station side). There is smoke billowing in the stadium," Cimini tweeted.

Video from those inside the stadium showed the smoke pouring over the stadium and onto the empty field.

An NJ Transit spokesperson told the New York Post that the fire didn’t affect service for the Meadowlands shuttle that sits adjacent to the stadium.

The fire came after the Jets lost its fifth straight game, where quarterback Geno Smith suffered multiple injuries that knocked him out of the game.

Smith had to go through concussion protocol after getting sandwiched between two Bills defenders, sending him crashing to the turf. He eventually returned after rookie Cade Klubnik held down the Jets’ offense in his place. However, Smith sustained an ankle injury that would take him out of the game completely.

Meanwhile, Josh Allen and the Bills had their way with the Jets. Allen finished with 196 yards passing with a touchdown and interception, while scoring twice on the ground. James Cook also rushed for 157 yards on 18 carries with a 74-yard touchdown run.

item.title: NFL legend's son makes incredible one-handed catch to help high school win championship in Pennsylvania
item.description: Jett Harrison's stunning one-handed catch helped St. Joseph's Prep win the Philadelphia Catholic League title against the school his father attended.

While sitting in front of a window, Laura began the weekly series with the intention to "continue the good work that was being established here in this Sunday service community."

item.title: Seahawks receiver Tory Horton made one of the smartest plays you'll ever see in Seattle's win over Las Vegas
item.description: Tory Horton's brilliant kickoff swat burned critical seconds off the clock and triggered the two-minute warning in the Seattle Seahawks' win.
item.content:encoded:
Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald is a Super Bowl champion for a reason. He's a damn good football coach. Perhaps nothing showed how well Seattle is coached quite like a play Seahawks receiver Tory Horton made in the final minutes.

With the Seahawks leading 21-10, Matt Gay kicked a 43-yard field goal to make it a one-score game. The Raiders had 2:04 on the clock and two timeouts left as they lined up for the ensuing kickoff, leaving them with a decision. They could attempt an onside kick or just kick it deep and play defense.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Las Vegas elected to kick it deep, but that brought another problem into play. If the Seahawks could burn at least four seconds off the clock during the kick return, it would take the game to the two-minute warning and eliminate one of the remaining clock stoppages.

So, the Raiders had two choices: kick the ball out of the back of the end zone or deliberately kick the ball out of bounds along the sideline. If the Raiders weren’t sure Gay could get it out the back, I think they should’ve kicked it out of bounds and lived with giving Seattle the ball at the 40. A touchback would’ve put Seattle at the 35.

Gay elected the former and booted the ball as far as he could. His kick sailed into the air and appeared headed out of the end zone. But that's when Horton made one of the smartest football plays I think I've ever seen.

HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL GAME ENDS WITH THREE LATERALS, A FOOLED DEFENSE & THE HIGHEST IQ PLAY YOU'LL EVER SEE

The Seahawks wide receiver leapt and swatted the kick before it could sail out the back of the end zone. Once the ball hit the ground, Horton immediately started pointing at teammate Rashid Shaheed, as if to say, "pick it up and run!"

Shaheed did exactly that, scooping up the ball in the end zone and returning it to the Seahawks’ 19-yard line. But, more importantly, he ran five seconds off the clock and brought the game to the two-minute warning. Macdonald came onto the field with a huge smile, celebrating and congratulating Horton for making the heads-up play.

WATCH:

After the play, officials huddled and spoke with Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak. According to the official gamebook, they flagged Horton for an illegal bat, and Las Vegas declined the penalty.

CBS rules analyst Gene Steratore said he didn’t think Horton’s play was illegal. The rulebook backs him up. Rule 12-5-1(b) prohibits batting a loose ball in the end zone after it has touched the ground. Horton swatted the kick before it ever hit the turf.

Seattle took over at its own 19 with 1:59 left. If Las Vegas had used both remaining timeouts on the first two downs and then stopped Seattle inbounds on third down, the Seahawks could have burned up to 40 seconds before punting. Drew Lock made that moot when he ran for 15 yards on second-and-11. He took three knees from there to finish off a 21-13 win.

Although it didn't end up mattering, Tory Horton deserves a ton of credit for one of the smartest plays I've ever seen a football player make.

And Seahawks special teams coordinator Jay Harbaugh probably deserves a raise, too.

item.title: Blinken warns US ground invasion of Iran would be 'absolute disaster' as Tehran escalates attacks
item.description: Former Secretary of State Antony Blinken warned a U.S. ground invasion of Iran would be an "absolute disaster" as Tehran launched drones at Bahrain.
item.content:encoded:
Former Secretary of State Antony Blinken warned Saturday that airstrikes alone may not eliminate Iran's weapons capabilities, but said a U.S. ground invasion would be an "absolute disaster."

Speaking at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi, Blinken, who served under President Biden, pointed to Iran's massive territory, population of roughly 90 million and ability to produce weapons deep inside the country as obstacles to any military campaign aimed at dismantling its arsenal.

"The weapons that it continues to produce are back far enough, the range is great enough that you can't just take everything out," Blinken said. "You'd probably have to have a land invasion of some kind to do that, which would be an absolute disaster."

TRUMP KEEPS SIGNALING AN END TO IRAN WAR, BUT EXPERT WARNS A CRUCIAL PIECE OF HIS STRATEGY IS MISSING

Blinken's warning came ahead of Iran claiming Sunday to have launched six drones at a U.S. military installation in Bahrain, while reports surfaced that neighboring Iraq faced concerns that its territory could be drawn into a potential American ground operation.

Bahrain said its air defenses blocked several Iranian aerial attacks Sunday, the first such interceptions since September.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it targeted a U.S. air defense radar system at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base with six drones in retaliation for what it described as "hostile US actions," according to Iranian state media, Reuters reported.

Bahraini officials said the drones were intercepted before reaching their targets.

IRAN HAS 'SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASED' EFFORTS TO TARGET AMERICANS ABROAD, US INTELLIGENCE MEMO WARNS

The latest escalation came amid further fighting in Yemen, where the Houthis made advances against Saudi-backed forces, raising additional concerns about the conflict spreading across the region.

Blinken warned that Iran retains the ability to widen the confrontation despite the United States' overwhelming conventional military superiority.

While Washington can "escalate vertically" by intensifying its bombing campaign, Blinken said, Tehran can "escalate horizontally" by targeting American military installations, regional allies and critical infrastructure, either directly or through allied armed groups.

"Even though we're much more powerful, that asymmetry in their ability to escalate horizontally as opposed to vertically is not to our advantage," Blinken said.

The former top diplomat also emphasized the geographic challenges facing U.S. forces.

"That coastline along the Strait of Hormuz goes on forever," Blinken said.

Iran is roughly four times the size of California, with a coastline and weapons production facilities that could complicate efforts to eliminate its military capabilities through air power alone.

TRUMP'S MOAB THREAT COULD PUT IRAN'S DEEPEST BUNKERS IN AMERICA'S CROSSHAIRS

Concerns about a potential ground operation have also intensified in neighboring Iraq, where officials have resisted proposals to sharply restrict trade and movement across the Iranian border.

Iran International reported that Tehran has become concerned that Iraqi territory could be used as a staging ground for a potential U.S. operation into southern Iran.

The Iraqi newspaper Al-Mada reported Nov. 9 that Iraq's prime minister privately briefed Shiite political leaders on an alleged American military plan involving a ground offensive, the outlet said.

In an interview with France 24 published Friday, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein had also warned that the region's unstable security environment could not continue indefinitely.

The current state of "no war and no peace" is unsustainable, Hussein said, warning that the confrontation "either goes towards peace or it goes towards war."

AFTER 47 YEARS OF CONFRONTING IRAN, DOES AMERICA HAVE A STRATEGY FOR ENDING THIS WAR?

Hussein also said Baghdad has a responsibility to pursue diplomatic mediation because Iraq has already been drawn into the conflict.

He pointed to recent outreach to Tehran, including discussions with Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

The Iraqi foreign minister also rejected a reported U.S. demand that Baghdad close all but two of its land border crossings with Iran, describing the proposed restrictions as "not possible" and "a kind of sanction against the Iraqi people."

The border dispute comes as U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) expands efforts to disrupt Iranian weapons shipments and illicit trade through Task Force Iron Gate.

CENTCOM announced the task force would coordinate with other U.S. agencies to prevent Iran from transporting advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials and illicit revenue across its land borders and the Caspian Sea.

Iraq shares a roughly 1,000-mile border with Iran.

item.title: NTSB details warning whistles and emergency orders before tanker collision capsized New Orleans riverboat
item.description: NTSB investigators detail warning whistles and emergency orders captured on the tanker's voyage recorder before the New Orleans riverboat collision.
item.content:encoded:
A tanker suffered a steering problem about two minutes before slamming into a docked New Orleans riverboat Friday, federal investigators said Sunday, detailing warning whistles, calls for help and emergency orders before the collision.

The Atlantic Asphalt was heading upriver near the Crescent City Connection Bridge at about 12:26 p.m. when its rudder remained turned to the right, sending the ship toward the Mississippi River’s east bank, National Transportation Safety Board senior marine accident investigator Bart Barnum said.

The tanker struck American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage at about 12:28 p.m. The riverboat capsized in about 22 minutes, according to preliminary information presented by the NTSB.

NEW ORLEANS BOAT CRASH CALLED ‘MIRACLE ON THE MISSISSIPPI’ AS EVERYONE IS ACCOUNTED FOR, OFFICIALS SAY

Investigators downloaded more than nine hours of data from the tanker’s voyage data recorder, including bridge audio, rudder angle, engine RPM, course and speed.

The recordings captured sounds consistent with the ship’s whistle, warnings and requests for assistance over its marine radio, commands to deploy anchors and emergency shiphandling orders, Barnum said.

11-NIGHT CARIBBEAN CRUISE ABRUPTLY CANCELED AFTER COAST GUARD DETAINS SHIP

Officials described the steering problem as a "steering casualty," but cautioned that the term does not establish what went wrong.

"It could be many different things. That is something that we are investigating very closely," Barnum said.

AT LEAST 6 PEOPLE INJURED AFTER BOSTON DUCK BOAT OVERTURNS NEAR ENTRANCE TO POPULAR TOURIST ATTRACTION

NTSB board member John DeLeeuw said investigators have data on the tanker’s speed but are still analyzing it before releasing it publicly. Video showed anchors were down, but investigators are still determining which ones were deployed and how far, he said.

The findings follow a frantic rescue effort that officials said left everyone aboard the American Heritage alive. Roughly 100 people were pulled from the Mississippi River, while responders evacuated more than 80 before the vessel overturned, Port of New Orleans Harbor Police Chief Melanie Montroll said Saturday.

TWO DEAD, INCLUDING INFANT, AFTER BOAT CAPSIZES IN NEW YORK HARBOR; 12 RESCUED

"This is a miracle. It is a literal miracle on the Mississippi," Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry said Friday.

Eight people remained hospitalized Saturday, including two in serious condition. The other six were stable, officials said.

FBI INVESTIGATES SUSPECTED HOMICIDE ABOARD MSC SEASCAPE CRUISE SHIP AFTER SUDDEN RETURN TO TEXAS

The NTSB said Sunday that 140 passengers and 50 crew members were aboard the riverboat, a total of 190.

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno also said the American Heritage’s captain was injured but stayed aboard until passengers and crew were accounted for, becoming the last person to leave.

MOM LOSES GRIP ON DAUGHTER AS PASSENGER FERRY CAPSIZES WITH 20 PEOPLE STILL MISSING

"Every moment of the critical time [Friday], he did not want to leave his ship," Moreno said Saturday.

Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said Saturday that crews were preparing to remove 16,000 gallons of fuel before salvage operations, warning that removing the capsized vessel could take weeks. DeLeeuw said Sunday that divers had been in the water, with salvage work overseen by the Coast Guard and salvage companies.

UNLICENSED NYC BOAT OPERATOR ALLEGEDLY IGNORED SAFETY WARNINGS BEFORE MOTHER, BABY DIED IN CAPSIZING: FEDS

Interviews with American Heritage crew members were underway Sunday. Interviews with the Atlantic Asphalt’s crew were scheduled to begin Monday and continue through the week, Barnum said.

The NTSB expects to release a preliminary report within about 30 days. Sunday’s briefing was its last planned on-site news conference, DeLeeuw said, with further updates to be posted online.

Fox News Digital's Brittany Miller contributed to this report.

item.title: Kirk Cousins and the Minnesota Vikings are reunited and it feels so good after win over Green Bay Packers
item.description: Kirk Cousins led the Minnesota Vikings to a dominant win at Lambeau Field, and his emotional reunion with Kevin O'Connell raises a big question.
item.content:encoded:
We found out a lot about Kirk Cousins and the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday because it is hard to add a new quarterback on a Tuesday, have him in full practices only two days during the week, and by week's end win a game in the same venue where he tore his Achilles three years ago.

All that happened Sunday when the Minnesota Vikings beat the Green Bay Packers.

But of all the things we learned from this game, maybe the most important is that Cousins and the Vikings maybe should not have broken up a couple of years ago.

Perhaps they shouldn't have gone looking for greener pastures, shouldn't have believed for better outcomes, should not have quit on each other and the pretty good thing they had.

VIKINGS ACQUIRE KIRK COUSINS FROM RAIDERS WHO TURN TO FERNANDO MENDOZA AS THEIR STARTING QB

The Vikings and Cousins are together again. They're reunited and after winning in Lambeau Field, and they both feel so good.

"It's been a blast to do ball with him again," coach Kevin O'Connell said afterward.

"Football's an emotional game, and my football journey goes way back, and, you know, there's been highs and lows," Cousins told reporters after the victory. "And there's more of the story to write up ahead, but the last three years since being here have been a tough three years.

"And, there's a lot of gratitude right now for being in this group again."

The story of the misguided direction perhaps began in 2023 when Cousins tore his Achilles at Lambeau Field. Unable to overcome the injury by delivering a good season in 2026, the Vikings and Cousins went their different directions in March of 2024.

Cousins went to the Atlanta Falcons as a high-priced free agent, believing he could ultimately finish his career there. But that changed weeks after signing him, the Falcons drafted Michael Penix Jr. in the first round of the draft and anointed the rookie their starter before that very season was over.

Cousins sat much of 2025, and then went to the Raiders last offseason knowing he was keeping the starter's seat warm for Fernando Mendoza. Little did he know that seat would be pulled out from under him last week.

MINNESOTA VIKINGS' SOFT BENCHING OF KYLER MURRAY LEADS TO CARSON WENTZ TAKING OVER AS NEW STARTING QB

The Vikings? They didn't move on from Cousins to live happily ever after.

When Cousins left in 2024, the Vikings thought replacing him wasn't an issue. They had found Sam Darnold in 2024, they were getting ready to draft J.J. McCarthy in the first round, and there was a certain arrogance within the organization that they could find someone, anyone, and turn him into a treasure.

VIKINGS QUARTERBACK BATTLE MEETS EXPECTED END AS KYLER MURRAY BEATS OUT JJ MCCARTHY FOR STARTING JOB

But then Darnold left. And McCarthy didn't work out. And Carson Wentz didn't work out, and Kyler Murray didn't work out earlier this season.

And after those missteps, the Vikings decided last week that Cousins was their best option once again – just as he'd been from 2018 to 2023.

And Cousin showed he's all of that in this one game.

Cousins was already an upgrade by the time the Vikings held a 20-0 lead in the third quarter and scored twice more when the Packers tried to rally.

And, yes, we know ... That is not exactly Super Bowl caliber quarterback play we saw from Cousins, because he did throw an interception and he still has to clean up some stuff.

But having Cousins at quarterback clearly raised the Vikings' hopes. Justin Jefferson played with energy again. The offense could run the ball better because the Packers had to respect the passing game.

And the defense that is among the best in the NFL sacked Jordan Love eight times – the most by any team in a game this season – because the unit was in the mostly unfamiliar spot of playing with a lead.

"I thought for one of the first times this year, we played complimentary football," O'Connell said.

Cousins was careful when it was over to remind everyone that the story of his return and this Vikings' season is not fully written. But we have a good start to the tale:

It begins with the fact this combination maybe would have been better off staying together.

item.title: TNA's Trey Miguel working his way to Canada for Destination X title match despite travel chaos

item.title: USC great Keyshawn Johnson calls for Lincoln Riley's job: 'Time to find somebody else'
item.description: Keyshawn Johnson posted a frustrated video calling for USC to fire Lincoln Riley after the Trojans' 27-13 loss to Indiana knocked them from CFP contention.
item.content:encoded:
The No. 18 USC Trojans would’ve helped their College Football Playoff chances if they could take down No. 9 Indiana on the road Saturday, but they were unable to muster second-half points in a 27-13 defeat.

Now, one Trojan legend is calling for head coach Lincoln Riley to be fired.

Keyshawn Johnson, the former wide receiver who went on to become a Super Bowl winner and three-time Pro Bowler in the NFL, posted a video on X where he was very frustrated with the result in Bloomington.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I tried my best, but in all honesty, though, it’s time to – you know what I mean? It’s just time to find somebody else," he said in the video.

"I’m sorry, man. I don’t even know what to say. Where did we go wrong here? It’s unbelievable. I just don’t even know what to say."

INDIANA HOOSIERS BOOST COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF HOPES WITH 27-13 WIN OVER USC TROJANS

Johnson added, "Fight On, I guess," but he isn’t in the biggest of USC spirits after the loss.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Things were going well in the game, as the Trojans and Hoosiers were tied at 10 apiece entering halftime. However, USC had just three points in the second half, while Indiana found their way to run away with it at home.

Riley and the Trojans were riding high after taking down Ohio State earlier this season, which propelled them upward in the CFP standings. They had the opportunity to continue moving up if they could pick up key wins along the way.

But this loss, which moved USC to 7-3 on the season, essentially knocks them out of contention for the CFP.

With yet another three-loss season at this point for Riley, the chatter will grow about his future with the program. In fact, it was already present before the Ohio State game began to change the conversation. That 30-18 victory at home had Trojans fans believing a late-season run could get them in position to get a chance to fight for a national title.

After Indiana, USC is set to face unranked Maryland, but they would’ve seen No. 4 UCLA in their final regular-season matchup, which had the chance to be a gamechanger.

Instead, USC is looking to finish the year strong now, and Riley, who was hired in November 2021, could be coaching his final games as the Trojans look ahead to next season.

item.title: Joe Biden calls Zelenskyy 'moody and stubborn,' questions his gratitude in new memoir
item.description: Joe Biden calls Volodymyr Zelenskyy "moody" and "not as grateful as I would have expected" in his forthcoming memoir, "Promise Me, America."
item.content:encoded:
Former President Joe Biden described Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as difficult in private and insufficiently grateful in a forthcoming memoir reviewed Friday by The Wall Street Journal, adding his assessment to a relationship President Donald Trump has also publicly criticized.

Zelenskyy "could be moody and stubborn in our private conversations, and not as grateful as I would have expected," Biden said in "Promise Me, America," according to the newspaper.

Zelenskyy previously addressed questions about his gratitude during a February 2025 interview with Fox News' Bret Baier on "Special Report," following his Oval Office clash with Trump and Vice President JD Vance. When Baier asked whether he owed Trump an apology, Zelenskyy emphasized his appreciation for American support.

"I'm thankful to President Trump and to Congress, bipartisan support, and I was always very thankful from all our people," Zelenskyy said.

TRUMP CALLS FOR UKRAINE TO REPLACE ZELENSKYY AFTER CLASH OVER RUSSIA DIESEL DEAL: 'GET A NEW PRESIDENT'

In a November interview with Fox News chief foreign correspondent Trey Yingst, Zelenskyy defended Ukraine’s strikes on Russian oil refineries despite objections from the Trump administration.

Biden’s memoir also addresses his handling of the presidential transition and his concerns about the incoming Trump administration’s approach to negotiations with Moscow.

According to the account, Trump’s team sought a letter authorizing direct negotiations with Russian President Vladimir Putin before Trump returned to office. Biden said he declined because of what he believed such talks could mean for Ukraine.

KUSHNER ENTERS UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AS TRUMP EYES SECURING SAFEGUARDS AGAINST ANOTHER RUSSIAN INVASION

He was "unwilling to give them carte blanche for what I expected would be a kind of surrender, at Ukraine's expense," Biden said.

The former president also offered a personal assessment of Putin’s behavior during their encounters, describing an effort to project disinterest.

Putin "liked to slouch during a meeting, feigning indifference, like a teenager," Biden said.

Biden’s criticism of Zelenskyy appears alongside a favorable assessment of the Ukrainian leader’s previous career. His acting background "turned out to be very good training," Biden said.

ZELENSKYY CAN LEVERAGE MOSCOW TIES FROM COMEDY DAYS TO MAKE PEACE DEAL, SAYS FORMER KEY AIDE

During Biden’s presidency, Ukraine’s requests included stronger air defenses, expanded weapons production and assistance disrupting Russian military logistics, according to a December 2023 account from Zelenskyy’s office. Before that White House meeting, Zelenskyy expressed appreciation for international assistance.

"I’d like to thank America and our partners for their support," Zelenskyy said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Biden subsequently announced additional assistance in September 2024, including $2.4 billion through the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative, another Patriot air defense battery and expanded training for Ukrainian F-16 pilots. His statement framed the measures as part of helping Ukraine defeat Russia’s invasion.

"The United States will provide Ukraine with the support it needs to win this war," Biden said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Zelenskyy for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: White House calls DC policies 'insanity' after 19-year-old gunman gets probation in shooting
item.description: A 19-year-old who prosecutors said fired more than 20 rounds into a D.C. neighborhood got probation, prompting the White House to slam the city's crime policies.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE – A 19-year-old who authorities say fired more than 20 rounds into a Washington, D.C., neighborhood and wounded a boy playing basketball has been released on probation, prompting the White House to denounce the city’s sentencing policies as "insanity."

Prosecutors wanted Darius Drew behind bars for five years. Instead, a judge suspended a two-year prison sentence and ordered 18 months of supervised probation under the Youth Rehabilitation Act, a D.C. law U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro had previously urged lawmakers to overhaul.

"The case illustrates the insanity of Washington, D.C.’s soft-on-crime policies that allow adults to receive just a slap on the wrist for dangerous crimes like firing twenty rounds of ammunition into the community," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital.

TRUMP’S DC LAW-AND-ORDER BLITZ MARKS ONE YEAR WITH EYE-POPPING HAUL OF SUSPECTS

"It is remarkable that even with these types of radical policies in place, President Trump’s Safe and Beautiful Task Force has been able to drive down violent crime in our nation’s capital," Bis added.

Superior Court Judge Jennifer Di Toro granted Drew sentencing treatment under the Youth Rehabilitation Act over the government’s objection, according to federal prosecutors. Drew pleaded guilty Aug. 10 to aggravated assault and carrying a pistol without a license.

CHAOTIC TEEN BRAWL GOES VIRAL AFTER TEEN TERROR PROMPTS US ATTORNEY PIRRO'S PLAN TO PROSECUTE PARENTS

He was released Friday after spending nearly six months in custody following his May 22 arrest. Prosecutors opposed his release as well as the use of the youth sentencing law.

The gunfire that put him there came from two locations in a Northwest Washington neighborhood, according to the government’s evidence.

MARYLAND MAN ACCUSED OF GIRL'S FATAL SHOOTING RELEASED FROM PRISON DAYS BEFORE

On May 11, Drew rode a Lime bike into an alley before surveillance video captured him firing at a parked car, prosecutors said. The ShotSpotter gunfire detection system registered 10 shots.

Seconds later, Drew fired toward a nearby house. A boy playing basketball at a recreation center was struck in the leg.

By the time the shooting stopped, Drew had fired more than 20 rounds into the community, prosecutors said. Investigators later found two firearms, ammunition and large amounts of suspected narcotics and marijuana at his home.

REPEAT OFFENDER ACCUSED OF SHOOTING NATIONAL GUARD MEMBER HAS LENGTHY HISTORY WITH THE LAW, RECORDS SHOW

The probation ruling echoes a warning Pirro delivered to the D.C. Council more than a year earlier. In an Aug. 6, 2025, letter, she urged lawmakers to overhaul the Youth Rehabilitation Act, citing a separate case in which another 19-year-old received probation after shooting someone in the chest aboard a Metrobus.

SENATOR TIM SHEEHY: SOFT-ON-CRIME JUDGES NEED CONSEQUENCES. THE JAIL ACT DELIVERS

The law, which the D.C. Council expanded in 2018, allows eligible offenders who committed crimes before turning 25 to receive sentences below otherwise applicable mandatory minimums and potentially have their convictions set aside, Pirro wrote. Murder and the most serious sexual abuse offenses are excluded.

In that separate case described in the 2025 letter, the 19-year-old pleaded guilty to two offenses carrying five-year mandatory minimums but received probation after four months in jail awaiting trial, according to Pirro’s letter.

SUSPECTED FLORIDA PUBLIX SLASHER WALKED FREE FROM COURT MONTHS EARLIER DESPITE VICTIM WARNINGS

"This sentence was a legal sentence only because he was sentenced under the YRA," she wrote.

Pirro argued the law needed changes to balance rehabilitation with accountability. Her office said 96% of defendants younger than 25 who received felony sentences in D.C. Superior Court from 2022 through 2024 were eligible for sentencing under the act.

FBI REPORTS 114% JUMP IN VIOLENT CRIME ARRESTS UNDER TRUMP COMPARED TO BIDEN’S FINAL MONTHS

The White House pointed to Trump’s Safe and Beautiful Task Force as its response to crime in the capital, saying the operation has made more than 19,000 arrests, including those of murderers, sex offenders, drug traffickers and other violent criminals.

Fox News Digital reached out to the D.C. Council and Judge Di Toro’s office for comment.

item.title: Common blood pressure drug helps more stroke survivors reach critical health target
item.description: The REDUCE trial found spironolactone lowered blood pressure by nearly eight points in stroke survivors, but key questions about prevention remain.
item.content:encoded:
A low-cost medication could help stroke survivors whose blood pressure remains elevated despite treatment, a new study suggests.

The research, known as the REDUCE trial, looked at whether adding spironolactone, a medication commonly known as a water pill, could help lower blood pressure after a stroke. The findings were presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions, Nov. 6-9, 2026, in Chicago.

Participants were split into two groups. One added spironolactone to their regular treatment, while the other continued with usual post-stroke care.

SIMPLE EXERCISE DONE JUST ONCE A WEEK COULD HELP LOWER BLOOD PRESSURE

Researchers tracked the participants' blood pressure at home over the following six months to determine whether adding the medication made a difference.

After three months, the top blood pressure number was nearly eight points lower on average among people taking spironolactone compared with those receiving usual care – about 126 versus 133, the study said.

More patients taking spironolactone also reached the recommended blood pressure goal of less than 130/80. That included 52% of those taking the medication compared with 30% receiving usual care.

"Lowering blood pressure is the most important step in preventing another stroke, yet many survivors struggle to reach recommended blood pressure targets after a stroke," study co-lead author Dr. Jordana Cohen, an associate professor of medicine and epidemiology at the University of Pennsylvania, said in a news release.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"When spironolactone was added to post-stroke care, we saw a meaningful drop in blood pressure that may lower the risk of future strokes and heart attacks," she added.

Dr. Alfred Joshua, a California-based board-certified emergency physician and former chief medical officer who was not involved in the research, said the findings are encouraging, but do not yet show that the medication prevents a subsequent stroke.

"We already know that controlling blood pressure lowers the risk of another stroke," Joshua told Fox News Digital. "This study measured blood pressure, so whether adding spironolactone leads to fewer repeat strokes is still an open question."

Spironolactone works by helping the body get rid of extra salt and water, which can lower blood pressure, according to the U.S. National Library of Medicine. It also causes the body to hold onto potassium, so patients taking it need to have their levels checked, the drug’s prescribing information states.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Joshua warned that high potassium is one of the main safety concerns because it can develop without symptoms. The risk can be higher for people with kidney problems and those taking certain medications or potassium supplements.

The medication can also lower blood pressure enough to cause dizziness, he added.

"If your blood pressure is still high after a stroke, bring your home readings to your clinician and ask whether this medication is a good fit," Joshua advised.

The trial ended early with 160 participants instead of the planned 200, and about 15% did not have blood pressure readings available at the three-month mark, the researchers noted.

People taking spironolactone were also taking slightly more blood pressure medications overall than those receiving usual care.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The study was not designed to determine whether spironolactone actually prevents another stroke or heart attack. Larger and longer studies are needed to answer that question, according to the researchers.

Fox News Digital reached out to the researchers for comment.
